_readme: ST-I3 · THE ONE VECTOR FOR THE HOME-CURRENCY RATE TABLE, read by BOTH ends of it:
services/platform/test/fx.test.ts   parses a hand-built document in the ECB's own format and
asserts the Worker stores and serves exactly `response`;
packages/core/test/money/fx_rates_test.dart  reads `response` into FxTable and asserts every
So a change to the payload's shape, or to how either side reads it, reddens the other side's test
too. `response` is the body of GET /v1/fx/latest and what CONFIG_KV holds under `fx:ecb:latest`.
⚠️ THE RATES ARE HAND-BUILT, NOT AN ECB PUBLICATION FOR THAT DATE. They are plausible magnitudes
and nothing else; no figure here is a claim about any real day's fix.
`conversions` go THROUGH EUR (units per one euro), in Money's wire shape, rounded HALF TO EVEN
into the target's minor units. fx.test.ts re-derives each `expect` from `response.rates` with
exact decimal arithmetic, so an edited rate with an unedited expectation is red on both sides.

response.source: Euro foreign exchange reference rates, European Central Bank

conversions.why: The headline case: ₹649 shown in dollars. 64900 × 1.1732 ÷ 103.987 = 732.21… cents.
The reverse cross: $10.00 in rupees. 1000 × 103.987 ÷ 1.1732 = 88635.36… paise.
Minor-unit digits differ: £10.00 in yen, which has none. 1000 × 173.52 ÷ 0.8731 ÷ 100 = 1987.40… yen.
Into the base itself: ₹649 in euros. 64900 ÷ 103.987 = 624.11… cents.
